title: Refactor presubmit artifact pruner and introduce dependency stewarding with lightweight runner
author: Aisha Menon
release_notes: Small refactor to presubmit runner and dep stewarding: reduced CI wall-time for lint by ~35% and added a dependency rotation/approval bot. Non-breaking runtime change.
description: Motivation: Presubmit latency and noisy dependency churn have been two recurring developer pain points. This PR refactors the presubmit artifact pruner to be stage-aware, introduces a lightweight presubmit runner that does fast lint+type checks for most PRs, and adds a Dependency Steward component (opt-in) that surfaces suspected dev-dep rot and creates curated rotation PRs. Summary of changes: - Stage-aware artifact pruner: pruner now prunes only artifacts for long-running lanes and preserves fastpath caches for tagged fast-lane PRs. This reduces redundant cache eviction and warms fastpath caches more reliably. - Lightweight presubmit runner: a small Go runner that executes a minimal lint/type subset using cached toolchains. New fastpath lane runs in ~30s on average for changed JS/TS/Go packages. - Dependency Steward: watches package lockfiles, runs a lightweight compatibility probe (matrix of latest patch/minor versions) and opens an automated PR template with suggested updates and risk tags. This component is opt-in via a repo label (deps/auto). - CI wiring and release hooks: composer for presubmit lanes adjusted to avoid running full integration matrix on docs-only or trivial changes; release smoke now runs only after merge in release lanes. - Observability: added presubmit-duration and dep-steward-created metrics, and a small dashboard link. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for pruner and runner - [x] E2E smoke in the fastpath lane - [x] Integration test for DepSteward probe harness - [x] Docs updated (devtools/presubmit.md) - [x] Linear tickets linked Implementation notes: commits are structured to separate the pruner refactor from the new runner and the dep steward. The runner is intentionally minimal; any heavy checks are still gated into the existing heavy-lane workflows. Security: DepSteward does not have write-by-default; it opens PRs and requires repo-level approval. The agent uses the existing bot user and KMS keys. Migration plan: rollout is staged: (1) enable fastpath lane for a small set of repos, (2) monitor presubmit-duration and CI failure modes for two weeks, (3) enable DepSteward on opt-in repos and monitor for false positives. Related: ENG-2142 (presubmit performance), ENG-3384 (dep rotation pilot). Links: internal doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2142/presubmit-fastpath-runner and design spec in docs/devtools/dep-steward.md.
